episode_title: Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats need to ‘earn’ their mandate | Newsmakers
script_en: Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats need to ‘earn’ their mandate | Newsmakers.
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed says Americans “temporarily” put their trust and hope in Democrats.
But he adds that if his party doesn’t act boldly when it takes control of Congress, it may lose that trust.
El-Sayed is the first Muslim to be elected to the U.S.

The 42-year-old progressive from Michigan is now calling for new Senate leadership and urging President Trump to meet and discuss how they can “figure out what we can work on and get done.” El-Sayed, a former Detroit public health official, even floated the idea of naming major healthcare legislation after Trump.
“Put his name on it,” El-Sayed said.

I don't care what it's called.” In this episode from NPR’s Newsmakers, El-Sayed sat down with NPR host Leila Fadel to talk about a divisive campaign season, the future of the Democratic Party and how Congress should legislate during the final two years of Trump’s term in the White House.
